ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 driver-cancellation (rider no-show) fee on RydeX; no voucher to the rider. Note the null driver_pressed_here_at field (F7) for data-quality review of the arrival-tap vs platform-auto-confirm logging, and advise the driver that the 17:19/17:22 chats (F10, F11) should be sent earlier in the wait window.

rejected_claims.reason: NS-0 does route a driver no-show cancellation into NS-1, but all three NS-1 elements pass on the record: tap/arrival at 17:18:50 (F6) with platform arrival logged at 17:17:50 (F5), 38 m from the pickup at the tap with a 34 m closest approach (F6, F1), and 3 min 40 s inside 200 m after the tap before the 17:22:30 cancellation (F6, F4). The framework holds but does not produce the refund the claim seeks [NS-0][NS-1].

F7 (null tap) conflicts with F6 (tap at 17:18:50), and F5 independently records a platform arrival; the more specific arrival record plus the driver's chat (F10) and statement (F12) make NS-1(i) satisfied, so the asserted failure is not established [F7][F6][F5][F10][F12][NS-1][NS-2].

NS-1(ii) is measured against the pickup radius, and the GPS record shows the driver inside 200 m from 17:17:50 for 4 min 40 s with a 34 m closest approach and a 53 m stationary hold (F2, F1, F3). Ryde publishes no arrival radius (gap G2), so 34–53 m satisfies 'at the pick-up location' [F2][F1][F3][NS-1].

NS-2 refunds the $6.61 only if an NS-1 element fails; (i) per F6/F5, (ii) per F1/F2/F3 and (iii) per F6/F4 all pass, so no refund arises and no NS-2 flag attaches (the driver was within range at the tap) [F6][F2][F1][F8][NS-1][NS-2].

The system records favour the driver here rather than the rider: F2 and F5 record arrival within 200 m and F6 records 3 min 40 s of waiting after the tap; the rider's own 'came out a minute after' account has no GPS or timeline fact behind it [F2][F5][F6][F12][NS-1].

The sequence is compliant, not contradictory: 200 m entered at 17:17:50 (F2), stationary hold from 17:18:25 (F3), arrival indication at 17:18:50 (F6), then 3 min 40 s and cancellation at 17:22:30 (F4) — the arrival indication and the wait both precede the cancellation [F2][F3][F6][F4][NS-1].

Traffic is irrelevant to a passenger-no-show cancellation: with no incidents or speed-band records and fair weather (F13, F14, F15), the driver cancelled on the NS-1 gateway, so NS-3 is not engaged and nothing external needs to excuse the fee [F13][F14][F15][NS-3].

Profile facts may only support an additional action and never decide the case; NS-2's flag requires the driver to have tapped 'I'm Here' while outside the pickup range, which F1/F2 refute, and the driver's 90-day record (F17, both no-show matters) does not trigger RD-6 because there is no RD-2 refund and no RD-1 breach here [F16][F17][F1][F2][NS-2][RD-6].

Withdrawn by the rider advocate; to the extent it argues the recorded tap time does not cure NS-1(i), the trace and F6 fix the tap at 17:18:50 with 3 min 40 s of subsequent waiting inside 200 m before the 17:22:30 cancellation, satisfying NS-1(iii) [F6][F7][F4][NS-1].
Accepted only as to the framework and the $6.61 figure; the claim adds nothing to the analysis since payment is governed by NS-1, whose elements are examined via C1–C9 [F4][F8][NS-0][NS-1].
